Live AGROVOC alignment for a vector of free-text terms

Source: R/causal_ontology.R
causal_ontology_agrovoc_align.Rd

For each input term, queries the AGROVOC SPARQL endpoint for concepts whose skos:prefLabel or skos:altLabel contains the term, ranks the matches by Levenshtein distance to the canonical label, and returns the best hit. Results are cached on disk via cache_path so that repeated runs over the same vocabulary do not re-query FAO.

Usage

causal_ontology_agrovoc_align(
  terms,
  cache_path = NULL,
  max_per_term = 5L,
  endpoint = "https://agrovoc.fao.org/sparql",
  timeout_sec = 60L,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

terms

Character vector of free-text terms (typically the nodes of a Knowledge Graph).

cache_path

Optional .rds file path. When supplied, the function reads cached matches on entry and writes updated matches on exit.

max_per_term

Integer — how many candidates to request per term (AGROVOC query LIMIT). The best one is kept.

endpoint

Override the SPARQL endpoint URL.

timeout_sec

Per-query timeout.

verbose

Logical — print one line per queried term.

Value

A data frame with columns term (input), uri (AGROVOC concept), label (AGROVOC pref label), distance (Levenshtein of lowercased label vs term).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  # Live SPARQL over HTTP: one round trip per uncached term, several
  # seconds each. Point `cache_path` at a location that survives the
  # session -- tempdir() is a fresh directory every time R starts, so
  # a cache written there never gets read back.
  cache <- "tools/.agrovoc_cache.rds"
  ag <- causal_ontology_agrovoc_align(
    c("soil organic carbon", "bulk density", "gibbsite"),
    cache_path = cache, verbose = TRUE
  )
  ag

  # `distance` is the Levenshtein distance between the AGROVOC pref
  # label and the query, not a confidence. Zero means the label
  # repeats the query verbatim; a large value means AGROVOC returned
  # a much longer label that merely contains the query as a
  # substring. Filter on it before trusting the mapping.
  subset(ag, !is.na(uri) & distance <= 3)

  # Failures are cached as well as hits, so an endpoint outage is
  # persisted as a permanent NA row and later runs will not retry it.
  # Delete the cache file after an outage.
  unlink(cache)

  # unique() is applied before the terms are lower-cased and trimmed,
  # so two spellings of one concept both survive it and the result
  # gains a duplicate row (only one query is sent -- the in-flight
  # cache absorbs the second). De-duplicate yourself if the row count
  # matters downstream.
  nrow(causal_ontology_agrovoc_align(c("gibbsite", "Gibbsite")))
} # }
